tldr: ZeroGUI is a scalable online learning framework that automates GUI Agent training at zero human cost through VLM-based automatic task generation, automatic reward estimation, and two-stage online reinforcement learning, significantly improving performance on OSWorld and AndroidLab.
contributions: Proposes ZeroGUI, a fully automated online training framework for GUI agents with zero human annotation cost
Introduces VLM-based automatic task generation that produces diverse training tasks from random initial states, including infeasible tasks
Introduces VLM-based automatic reward estimation using a voting mechanism to reduce false positives
Adapts GRPO to multi-step trajectories with a modified KL loss term for improved training stability
Demonstrates significant performance gains on two advanced GUI agents (UI-TARS and Aguvis) across desktop and mobile environments
methods: ZeroGUI operates as a Markov Decision Process where GUI agents interact with environments through screenshots. It uses GPT-4o to generate training tasks (10 tasks per step for OSWorld, 5 for AndroidLab) via example-guided prompting and multi-candidate generation, including intentionally infeasible tasks. Reward estimation uses Qwen2.5-VL-32B queried 4 times with unanimous agreement voting, excluding agent responses to avoid hallucination-driven false positives. Two-stage online RL extends GRPO to multi-step trajectories, normalizing rewards within groups for advantage estimation, and replaces the k3-estimator KL loss with a k2-estimator (per-token MSE) for stability. Training used group size G=64, KL coefficient β=0.1, AdamW with learning rate 2e-6, and DAPO dynamic sampling.
results: On OSWorld feasible subset: ZeroGUI-UI-TARS-7B achieves +4.5 absolute (+40% relative) improvement; ZeroGUI-Aguvis-7B achieves +2.1 absolute (+88% relative) improvement. On full OSWorld test set: UI-TARS-7B improves +2.5 absolute (+14% relative), Aguvis-7B improves +1.9 absolute (+63% relative). Generated task training significantly improves pass@4 (capability coverage), while test-time training primarily boosts all-pass@4 (consistency). More than 4,000 Ubuntu-based tasks and 225 Android-based tasks were generated, with 725 Ubuntu and 175 Android tasks sampled for training (approximately twice the test set size).
limitations: VLM-based reward estimation is imperfect and may produce false positives or false negatives, with false positives having greater impact on policy improvement
Relies on screenshot-only evaluation mode; XML or SoM modes were not tested
GPT-based evaluation for certain AndroidLab query-detecting tasks is noted as not fully reliable
The two-stage approach requires additional computational cost for VLM-based task generation and reward estimation at each step
Training stability improvements required modifying the KL loss term, suggesting the original GRPO formulation is not directly applicable to multi-step GUI interaction settings
